documents.title: Academic Integrity for Students
documents.summary: University GenAI guidance for students: no campus-wide rules on permissible AI use, the professor decides, and students must get permission or assume AI is not allowed when silent. Points to the Academic Honesty Policy, privacy policy and Honor Code, and lists department statements.
documents.stance_why: The page says BYU has no school-wide policy and the professor is 'the arbiter', but it sets a university-wide fallback: students 'must ask your professor for permission' and 'assume that using GenAI is not permitted' if the syllabus is silent. That is a ban unless permitted, so restrict rather than delegates.

units.why: States that the university has no school-wide AI rule, so the decision sits below the university; this is informational and fits the 'who decides' type, not a framework type.

units.policy: BYU has no specific school-wide policies defining permissible AI use for assignments, tests, or other schoolwork.

documents.stance_why: The memo says AI use 'should be consistent with' the Honor Code and Academic Honesty Policy and that 'specific guidelines' are left to colleges, departments and faculty; it sets no stance and explicitly rejects a ban.

documents.title: ECEn Policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Coursework
documents.summary: ECEn departmental default AI policy for ECEn and IT&C classes, in force when an instructor is silent. It frames AI as a professional skill, bars use on closed-book work and where it circumvents learning, requires citation, lists appropriate uses, and leaves penalties to the instructor.
documents.stance_why: The policy allows AI by default for coursework, with conditions: cite it, do not use it on closed-book work or to circumvent learning, and follow instructor rules. It names appropriate uses and is not a ban or a tier menu, so permit.

units.why: It is the default for all ECEn and IT&C classes 'unless superseded' by the instructor, a default-rule statement; P06 over P04 because the point is what applies by default.
